# Negative minimum-dispersion credit at an actual critical cap cover
unconditional nonnegative credit in the new three-cap aggregation
formula. The actual depth here is ABOVE OC. It therefore does not
refute a credit estimate conditional on a bad depth minimum, and it
is not a counterexample to OC.

## Actual convex source and its exact maximum depth

In R x R^2 put

    C={ (z,x,y): -1<=z<=1, |x-z/2|<=1, |y|<=1 }.

This is a full-dimensional compact parallelepiped. Its integer bases
are -1,0,1, with fibers

    K_z=[z/2-1,z/2+1] x [-1,1].

Every fiber has area4, total mixed area M=12, and the source S is
centrally symmetric about o=(0,0,0), which belongs to its middle fiber.
For every closed halfspace through o, symmetry shows its mass is at
least M/2=6, including a possible positive boundary mass. A containing
halfspace includes its parallel through-o halfspace and has no less
mass. Conversely, at any candidate point, the two opposite halfspaces
through that point with continuous normal (1,0) have boundary of mixed
area zero and masses summing to M. One has mass at most6. Therefore

    max_{w in S} raw_depth(w)=6,
    max_{w in S} normalized_depth(w)=1/2.

No restriction to continuous-only directions is used for the lower
bound; central symmetry handles every oblique ambient halfspace.

## A genuine critical three-cap circuit

Use the ambient closed caps

    H_1={x>=0},       H_2={y>=0},       H_3={x+y<=0}.

Their three continuous normals form a positive circuit. Their margins
x,y,-x-y sum to zero, so the caps cover the whole ambient space and
have a common boundary point o. Central symmetry and boundary-nullness
give each cap the exact mixed mass B=6. Thus all three are genuinely
active depth-minimizing caps at the globally deepest point o. This is
one valid circuit group, anchored at the integer base zero, whose
projected covering set contains all three bases.

Every cap cuts a positive proper area from EVERY fiber. Direct rectangle
integration gives the following table (columns are cap indices):

    z=-1:    1, 2, 23/8,
    z= 0:    2, 2, 2,
    z= 1:    3, 2, 9/8.

For example, in the first fiber the third cap has a full height-two
strip for -3/2<=x<=-1 and height1-x for -1<=x<=1/2. Its area is
1+integral_(-1)^(1/2)(1-x)dx=23/8. Symmetry gives the final9/8.
Each column sums to6.

## The cross-capture credit is strictly negative

Assign every fiber to this single group. In the notation of the
rank-two three-cap overlap aggregation theorem, the outside-capture
sum is X=0 and the retained pointwise minimum sum is

    L=1+2+9/8=33/8.

The minimum-dispersion deficit and planar overlap coefficient are

    Delta=B-L=15/8,             r=3/4.

Consequently the proposed unconditional sign is false:

    X-r Delta= -45/32 <0.

This failure retains actual convex fibers, a complete integer base,
equal GLOBAL cap budgets, positive proper traces on every fiber,
true active caps, a single deterministic globally deepest anchor,
and a positive normal circuit. It does not rely on arbitrary unrelated
cap arrays or on noncritical caps.

The omitted local overlap surplus explains why there is no depth
contradiction. At the three fibers, the exact nonnegative differences

    E_z=sum_j |K_z intersect H_j|-|K_z|-r min_j|K_z intersect H_j|

are9/8,1/2,41/32, respectively, summing to93/32. The full accounting
identity is

    (3-r)B = M + X-r Delta + sum_z E_z
           = 12-45/32+93/32 =27/2.

Thus keeping the actual overlap surplus restores a positive net credit
here. An argument that bounds it below in terms of dispersion must
state and prove the additional geometric premise. In particular the
present example does not settle any such estimate in the regime
beta<Gamma_d/2^n or at a local minimum over convex source bodies.
